description: Hi everyone! I'm a tech enthusiast who loves diving into complex challenges and turning rough ideas into working prototypes. My main interests are problem-solving, building practical tech solutions, and figuring out the smartest way to tackle tricky logic under a tight deadline. I enjoy the fast pace of hackathons and keeping the team focused on delivering a solid, functional project.
summary:
ARES STATION – NASA Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

ARES STATION is an interactive Mars survival simulator designed to introduce players to the challenges of living and working on Mars. In this experience, players take on the role of astronauts stranded on the Martian surface after a missed battery rendezvous. Their mission is to keep the station operational and ensure the crew's survival until a rescue mission arrives on Sol 16.

Players explore the Martian environment, complete missions and manage essential resources such as oxygen, electricity, food and health. They must make important decisions, respond to unexpected challenges and maintain the station's critical life-support systems. The game features a six-chapter storyline that gradually introduces new challenges and makes the survival experience more engaging.

The project combines space science, interactive storytelling and problem-solving into one educational experience. It introduces players to important concepts such as renewable energy, resource management, life-support technology and the difficulties of human exploration beyond Earth.

ARES STATION aims to make learning about Mars more exciting by allowing players to experience the responsibilities of an astronaut rather than simply reading about them. It encourages curiosity, critical thinking and scientific awareness while inspiring young learners to explore the possibilities of future human missions to Mars.
details:
ARES STATION Mission Trainer ARES STATION is a 3D, first-person Mars survival simulator where players take the role of astronauts operating a remote Martian outpost. The objective is to survive for 16 Martian days (Sols) until a rescue mission arrives. Players must carefully manage essential resources, including oxygen, electricity, food, health and shielding, while completing missions and responding to unexpected events.

The game features an interactive Martian environment, touchscreen joystick controls, station terminal operations, resource management and a six-chapter storyline. Player decisions affect resource availability and survival, creating different challenges and possible success or failure outcomes. Solar energy is generated automatically, while accumulated dust reduces the panels' efficiency.

The project was developed as a browser-based game using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Three.js for 3D graphics. It is designed to run in a web browser and can be accessed through a website link. The main benefit is its educational approach to space exploration. Instead of simply reading about astronauts, players experience the importance of scientific decision-making, renewable energy, resource conservation and life-support systems. Our creative approach was to combine a realistic survival challenge with an engaging story mode. During development, we considered gameplay difficulty, resource balance, accessibility, scientific relevance and player engagement. We wanted the experience to be challenging without becoming unnecessarily complicated. The intended impact is to inspire young learners to explore space science, develop problem-solving skills and understand the challenges of future human missions to Mars.
